title: Demons
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Demons are evil spiritual beings who oppose God, deceive people, and serve satanic purposes. They are real, but they remain created beings under God’s authority and beneath Christ’s power.
summary: Demons are evil spiritual beings who oppose God, deceive people, and serve satanic purposes. They are real, but they remain created beings under God’s authority and beneath Christ’s power.
christFocus: Jesus Christ has absolute authority over demons. His ministry displays the arrival of God’s kingdom and His power to deliver those oppressed by darkness.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture teaches that demons are real spiritual enemies. They know truth in a limited way, tremble before God, deceive, oppress, and oppose the work of Christ.

Demons are not myths, symbols of human weakness, or powers equal with God. They are evil created beings under limitation and judgment. Their activity is serious, but never ultimate.

Jesus repeatedly demonstrated authority over demons. He commanded them, silenced them, and delivered people from their oppression. The kingdom of God breaks into darkness through His authority.

Believers must avoid both denial and obsession. Scripture gives enough truth to stand firm, resist deception, and trust Christ without building faith around demonic fascination.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people explain every struggle as demonic, while others deny demonic reality altogether. Both can leave people unprepared. Scripture calls believers to sober truth.

This doctrine offers hope to those afraid of spiritual evil. Demons are real, but Christ is stronger. No demon is equal to the Lord who commands them.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Take demonic evil seriously without making it the center of your faith. Stay grounded in Scripture, reject superstition, pray with dependence, and trust Christ’s authority. When spiritual bondage or oppression is suspected, seek wise, biblically grounded pastoral help rather than fear-driven speculation.
